text:
Detroit spent two periods playing the better hockey and still trailed, and by the third the gap had closed in the other direction. The Rangers outshot the Red Wings in expected goals 1.45 to 0.08 in the final period, and Eeli Tolvanen turned that squeeze into the insurance goal at 18:44, a wrist shot from a 57 percent look. It made the final NYR 2, DET 0.

The first goal was the unlikelier one. Sean Durzi scored on a power-play slap shot at 5:12 of the first, off an 8 percent chance, with Gabe Perreault and Will Cuylle assisting. Detroit then carried the period, 1.03 expected goals to 0.73, and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård had the best look of the night for either side, a 33 percent chance that Dylan Garand stopped. Garand finished with 22 saves on 22 shots, 1.7 goals better than the chances he faced, and was named first star.

Over the full game the Rangers did hold the edge in chance quality, 3.02 expected goals to 1.7, but a good chunk of that came on special teams (0.74 from their four power plays) and in that final period. At even strength it was dead level, 1.37 to 1.36, and shot attempts favored Detroit 45 to 43. John Gibson was solid too, stopping 19 of 20 for 1.12 goals saved above expected. By the numbers the Rangers deserved the win 58 percent of the time, so the result fit the chances, even if the middle of the game did not.
